cguCitoyen.title: Terms of use — individuals
cguCitoyen.intro: These terms apply to anyone who uses AccesDirectAide for themselves, with or without an account.
cguCitoyen.operator.title: 1. Who provides the service
cguCitoyen.operator.p1: The service is provided by {{operator}}, a natural person, who operates AccesDirectAide in a personal, voluntary capacity. No association has been created to date.
cguCitoyen.free.title: 2. A free service
cguCitoyen.free.p1: The service is free. No payment is asked of you, either by AccesDirectAide or, through it, by a structure. The site contains no advertising.
cguCitoyen.noDecision.title: 3. What the service does not do
cguCitoyen.noDecision.p1: AccesDirectAide is not a government website. It helps you find information, check whether an aid may concern you and contact a structure. It takes no decision on your rights: only the competent body (Caf, CPAM, France Travail, Collectivité européenne d'Alsace, CCAS…) decides.
cguCitoyen.noDecision.p2: The information is given for guidance, with its official source and its date. It may change: check it with the source shown.
cguCitoyen.ai.title: 4. The automatic assistant (not open yet)
cguCitoyen.ai.p1: The automatic assistant is not open yet. When it is, it will be able to search, explain and suggest a draft. It may make mistakes. It will not give legal advice and will decide nothing.
cguCitoyen.ai.p2: Once it is open, do not write in it any information about your health, a disability, your administrative situation or that of another person.
cguCitoyen.account.title: 5. Your account
cguCitoyen.account.i1: An account gives you access to your personal space (My Space). It will be needed to request an appointment once that function opens; it is not open yet.
cguCitoyen.account.i2: You must be 18 or over to create an account.
cguCitoyen.account.i3: You give accurate information and keep your password secret.
cguCitoyen.account.i4: Your account is personal: do not act on behalf of another person without their agreement.
cguCitoyen.appointments.title: 6. Appointments (not open yet)
cguCitoyen.appointments.p1: Appointment requests are not open yet. The rules below will apply once they are; these terms will then be updated and account holders will be informed.
cguCitoyen.appointments.p2: An appointment request will not be a confirmed appointment: the structure will confirm, offer another slot or decline. It will also be able to change or cancel an appointment; you will be informed in your space.
cguCitoyen.appointments.p3: You will be able to cancel your request or your appointment from your space. You will need to give notice as early as possible.
cguCitoyen.appointments.p4: Each structure sets its own reception rules. AccesDirectAide guarantees neither an available place nor the granting of an aid.
cguCitoyen.appointments.p5: The message attached to a request will be optional. It will only be passed on with your agreement, which you will be able to withdraw at any time from your space.
cguCitoyen.use.title: 7. Proper use
cguCitoyen.use.i1: Do not publish or send content that is unlawful, abusive or harmful to another person.
cguCitoyen.use.i2: Do not try to access other people's data or to disrupt the service.
cguCitoyen.use.i3: Do not use a program to extract content in bulk or to use a function of the service automatically, including, once it opens, the booking of slots.
cguCitoyen.deletion.title: 8. Deleting your account
cguCitoyen.deletion.p1: You can ask for your account to be deleted at any time, from your space or by writing to {{contact}}. A person checks the request before deletion, to avoid a mistake or identity theft.
cguCitoyen.deletion.p2: Some data may be kept for a limited period when an obligation or the defence of a right requires it; the privacy notice lists them.
cguCitoyen.deletion.p3: If the account is used in breach of these terms, it may be suspended. You are informed of the reason, except in a security emergency, and you can submit your comments.
cguCitoyen.liability.title: 9. Liability
cguCitoyen.liability.p1: The operator takes reasonable steps to keep the information accurate and the service available. They cannot guarantee that there is no error at all or that the service runs without interruption. Reported errors are corrected as soon as possible.
cguCitoyen.liability.p2: The operator is not responsible for the decisions of public bodies and structures, nor for the content of the external sites they link to.
cguCitoyen.liability.p3: The operator remains liable for their own faults under the conditions laid down by law. No clause of these terms reduces the rights the law gives you.
cguCitoyen.changes.title: 10. Changes and end of the service
cguCitoyen.changes.p1: These terms may change. Each version is published with its date. Before a significant change, account holders are informed and can delete their account.
cguCitoyen.changes.p2: If the service stops or is taken over by someone else, for example an association created later, account holders are informed in advance. No data is passed on without prior information.
cguCitoyen.law.title: 11. Applicable law and disputes
cguCitoyen.law.p1: These terms are governed by French law. If there is a problem, first write to {{contact}}: an amicable solution is sought.
cguCitoyen.law.p2: Consumer mediation: whether it applies to a free service published by a private individual, outside any professional activity, remains to be checked. No mediator has been appointed to date.
cguCitoyen.law.p3: Failing an amicable solution, you may bring the matter before the competent court under the ordinary rules.
cguCitoyen.law.p4: Only the French version of these terms is legally authoritative; translations are an aid to understanding.
cguPro.title: Terms of use — professionals
cguPro.intro: These terms apply to professionals who use an ADA Pro account created at the invitation of their structure.
cguPro.intro_v9: These terms apply to professionals who use an ADA Pro account, created at the invitation of an administrator of their structure or of the operator.
cguPro.operator.title: 1. Who provides the service
cguPro.operator.p1: The service is provided by {{operator}}, a natural person, who operates AccesDirectAide in a personal, voluntary capacity. No association has been created to date. Contact: {{contact}}.
cguPro.operator.p2: The service is free for professionals and for their structure. Nothing is invoiced.
cguPro.account.title: 2. Your professional account
cguPro.account.i1: The account is created at the invitation of your structure. It is personal: do not share it.
cguPro.account.i1_v9: The account is created through an invitation sent to your professional e-mail address by an administrator of your structure or by the operator (for example for the first administrator of a structure). It is personal: do not share it.
cguPro.account.i2: Two-factor authentication is mandatory. Keep your sign-in means secret.
cguPro.account.i3: Your structure manages its team's access and deactivates your account when you leave it.
cguPro.use.title: 3. Use in the service of people
cguPro.use.i1: Use the account only for the tasks of your structure.
cguPro.use.i2: Open a person's information only when it is necessary for their request.
cguPro.use.i3: Do not copy this information outside the tools provided by your structure.
cguPro.use.i4: Respect professional secrecy and the rules of your structure.
cguPro.use.i5: Do not write health or disability data in a free-text field unless it is essential to the request.
cguPro.appointments.title: 4. Appointments
cguPro.appointments.p1: You confirm, offer another slot or decline the requests addressed to you, within a reasonable time. Keep your slots up to date.
cguPro.appointments.p1_v8: Appointment booking is not open yet. Once it is open for your structure, you confirm, offer another slot or decline the requests addressed to you, within a reasonable time, and you keep your slots up to date.
cguPro.appointments.p2: Neither the platform nor its assistant decides any right. A draft suggested by the assistant must be checked before any use.
cguPro.appointments.p2_v8: The platform decides no right: only the competent body decides.
cguPro.appointments.p3_v9: If video conferencing is activated for your structure (it is not today), its processing and its provider are described in the privacy notice.
cguPro.data.title: 5. Your own data
cguPro.data.p1: For your account, the platform processes your name, your professional e-mail address, your role, your slots and the log of your actions. The privacy notice describes this processing, its proposed legal bases and its retention periods.
cguPro.data.p1_v8: For your account, the platform processes your professional e-mail address, your role, your structure, your password in hashed (irreversible) form, the secret of your two-factor authentication, the log of your actions and your notification preferences. Once appointment booking is open for your structure, it also processes your slots. The privacy notice describes this processing, its proposed legal bases and its retention periods.
cguPro.data.p1_v9: For your account, the platform processes your professional e-mail address, your role, your structure, your password in hashed (irreversible) form, the secret of your two-factor authentication, the log of your actions and your notification preferences, as well as, if you enter them, your display name and job title. Once appointment booking is open for your structure, it also processes your slots. This processing is based on the performance of these terms (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR) and, for account security and the log of actions, on the legitimate interest of the operator and of your structure in protecting access (Article 6(1)(f)). The privacy notice describes it (section 3, P4p), with its retention periods (section 4) and how to exercise your rights (section 8).
cguPro.data.p2: Your actions are logged for security and access control.
cguPro.incident.title: 6. Security incident
cguPro.incident.p1: Report without delay to {{contact}} any loss of a sign-in means, any suspicious access or any sending error.
cguPro.end.title: 7. Suspension and end
cguPro.end.p1: If the account is used in breach of these terms, it may be suspended. You and your structure are informed, except in a security emergency.
cguPro.end.p1_v9: If the account is used in breach of these terms or in a security incident, your structure's administrator or the operator may disable your account: your sessions end at once. No automatic notice is sent to you when your account is disabled.
cguPro.end.p2_v9: A disabled account is kept for 12 months at most, so that it can be reactivated and actions can be proven, then erased by the operator; this erasure is not automated yet. You can ask for an earlier erasure by writing to {{contact}}. When your structure's space is closed, the accounts of its team are erased in the same way. The proof of your acceptance of these terms (account identifier, document, version and date, without your address) is kept for 12 months after the erasure; this deletion is not automated yet.
cguPro.liability.title: 8. Liability and applicable law
cguPro.liability.p1: Each party is liable for its own faults under the conditions laid down by law. The operator is not responsible for the decisions of your structure or of public bodies.
cguPro.liability.p2: These terms are governed by French law. If there is a problem, first write to {{contact}}.
cguPro.liability.p3: Only the French version of these terms is legally authoritative; translations are an aid to understanding.
structures.title: Conditions for structures
structures.intro: These conditions describe the rules proposed to structures (associations, public services, establishments) that appear in the directory or receive appointment requests. No structure has signed them to date.
structures.intro_v8: These conditions describe the rules proposed to structures (associations, public services, establishments) that appear in the directory, whose team uses ADA Pro accounts or that will receive appointment requests once this function is open; it is not open yet. No structure has signed them to date.
structures.directory.title: 1. Directory listing
structures.directory.p1: Listings come from official or public sources: FINESS, data·inclusion, the Annuaire de l'administration (Service-Public / DILA). Each listing shows its source and its date.
structures.directory.p2: A listing indicates that a service exists. It guarantees neither a place nor an admission.
structures.directory.p3: The structure can ask for its listing to be corrected or updated at {{contact}}.
structures.agreement.title: 2. Connection to appointments
structures.agreement.p1: To receive appointment requests, a written agreement is signed between the structure and the operator. It names a contact person. The connection is free: no sum is paid by the structure or to the structure.
structures.agreement.p1_v8: Appointment booking is not open yet. Once it is, a structure will receive appointment requests only after a written agreement with the operator has been signed, which will name a contact person. The connection will be free: no sum will be paid by the structure or to the structure.
structures.agreement.p2: The operator is {{operator}}, a natural person, who operates AccesDirectAide in a personal, voluntary capacity. No association has been created to date. Contact: {{contact}}.
structures.roles.title: 3. Roles for personal data
structures.roles.p1: For what it receives (requests, contact details, message accepted by the person), the structure is the controller of its own processing, in its own files and according to its own obligations.
structures.roles.p1_v8: Once appointment booking is open, the structure will be the controller of its own processing for what it receives (requests, contact details, message accepted by the person), in its own files and according to its own obligations.
structures.roles.p2: For the handling of the request in the platform, the operator and the structure would be joint controllers (GDPR, art. 26). An arrangement will set this out; its essence will be made available to the people concerned.
structures.roles.p3: If the structure uses the tool as its own diary, the operator would act as a processor (GDPR, art. 28), under a written contract.
structures.commitments.title: 4. Commitments of the structure
structures.commitments.i1: Answer requests within a reasonable time and keep its slots up to date.
structures.commitments.i1_v8: Once appointment booking is open: answer requests within a reasonable time and keep its slots up to date.
structures.commitments.i2: Manage its team's accounts: invite, remove rights and deactivate an account when a person leaves.
structures.commitments.i3: Inform people as its own obligations require.
structures.commitments.i4: Declare, before opening, the services whose nature may reveal health or disability data.
structures.commitments.i5: Apply a person's withdrawal of their agreement to the message: delete any copy, or keep it under its own responsibility and inform the person.
structures.commitments.i5_v8: Once the message attached to a request is open: apply a person's withdrawal of their agreement to that message, that is, delete any copy, or keep it under its own responsibility and inform the person.
structures.sensitive.title: 5. Sensitive services
structures.sensitive.p1: Booking services whose nature may reveal health or disability data is closed to date. Opening it requires a « service sensible » indicator, the person's explicit consent and a check of the requirements for hosting health data (to be checked).
structures.operatorCommitments.title: 6. Commitments of the operator
structures.operatorCommitments.i1: Provide the service free of charge, with appropriate security measures.
structures.operatorCommitments.i2: Inform the structure without undue delay of any incident affecting the data that concern it.
structures.operatorCommitments.i3: Not use these data for other purposes and never sell them.
structures.end.title: 7. Duration, end and applicable law
structures.end.p1: Either party may end the connection with the notice period set in the agreement. At the end, the data are returned or deleted as the agreement provides.
structures.end.p2: Each party is liable for its own faults. These conditions are governed by French law; an amicable solution is sought first.
structures.end.p3: Only the French version of these conditions is legally authoritative; translations are an aid to understanding.
privacyNotice.title: Privacy notice (GDPR, articles 13 and 14)
privacyNotice.intro: This notice explains which personal data AccesDirectAide processes, why, on what basis, for how long, and what your rights are.
privacyNotice.controller.title: 1. Controller
privacyNotice.controller.p1: The controller is {{controller}}, a natural person, who operates AccesDirectAide in a personal, voluntary capacity. No association has been created to date. No data protection officer has been appointed.
privacyNotice.controller.p2: For your data: write to {{contact}}. Several rights can also be exercised directly from your space (section 8).
privacyNotice.status.title: 2. Status of this notice
privacyNotice.status.p1: This notice describes the processing for personal accounts (section 3). Appointments, messages, reminders and the sharing of files are not open yet: their legal bases are given as proposals (section 3a) and will be confirmed before they open.
privacyNotice.status.p1_v9: This notice describes the processing for personal accounts (section 3) and for ADA Pro professional accounts (section 3, P4p, and section 11). In ADA Pro, only the account, team and structure-record functions are open (with the structure's log and statistics): the functions that would process information about the people being supported are closed. Appointments, messages, reminders, referrals between professionals and the sharing of files are not open yet: their legal bases are given as proposals (section 3a) and will be confirmed before they open.
privacyNotice.purposes.title: 3. Purposes and legal bases for personal accounts
privacyNotice.purposes.title_v9: 3. Purposes and legal bases for personal and professional accounts
privacyNotice.purposes.i1: P1 — Operation and security of the public site (technical logs, request rate limiting, security cookie « __csrf »): legitimate interest (art. 6(1)(f)).
privacyNotice.purposes.i2: P2 — Creating and keeping the account (verified e-mail address, protected password, « 18 or over » statement, proof of acceptance of the terms of use and of their version): performance of the contract formed by the terms of use (art. 6(1)(b)), for the data needed for the account only. Accepting the terms and the adult statement are not consents within the meaning of the GDPR. No telephone number is asked.
privacyNotice.purposes.i3: P2b — Optional display settings (text size, contrast, reduced animations, read aloud, easy-to-read French (FALC)): they are saved only in your browser, on your device (local storage). They are not sent to AccesDirectAide and are not saved in your account: we do not receive them. They therefore do not sync between your devices; on another device or browser you need to choose them again. They stay on the device after you sign out. You can change or reset them at any time (« Reset the display »), or erase them with your browser data. They are used only for the display you chose: they say nothing about your health or a disability, and no such information is asked. This storage on your device, made at your request to adapt the display, is not subject to a consent request (article 82 of the French Data Protection Act, « loi Informatique et Libertés »).
privacyNotice.purposes.i4: P3 — Sign-in and locking after several failed attempts: performance of the contract (art. 6(1)(b)) for signing in; legitimate interest in protecting accounts (art. 6(1)(f)) for the security measures.
privacyNotice.purposes.p4p_v9: P4p — ADA Pro professional accounts (creation by invitation, sign-in with mandatory two-factor authentication, management of the team and invitations by the structure administrator, proposals to update the structure's record, optional display name and job title, notifications and service e-mails, log of actions): performance of the terms of use for professionals accepted at sign-up (Art. 6(1)(b)); account security and log of actions: legitimate interest of the operator and of the structure in protecting access (Art. 6(1)(f)).
privacyNotice.purposes.i5: P10a — Service e-mails about the account (address verification, password, change of address, account notices): performance of the contract (art. 6(1)(b)).
privacyNotice.purposes.i6: P12 — Log of administration actions: legitimate interest (art. 6(1)(f)).
privacyNotice.purposes.i7: P13 — Exercise of your rights: legal obligation (art. 6(1)(c); articles 12 to 22 of the GDPR). Blocked retention (« hold ») of a specific piece of data: legal obligation when an authority or a court requires it (art. 6(1)(c)); otherwise, to establish, exercise or defend a legal claim, legitimate interest (art. 6(1)(f)) and, for sensitive data, art. 9(2)(f) — restricted access, duration limited to the dispute.
privacyNotice.purposes.i9: P15 — Erasure when the periods end: legal obligation (art. 6(1)(c); art. 5(1)(e) and 17 of the GDPR). Proof archives with restricted access (for example the proof of a consent or of a rights request): legitimate interest (art. 6(1)(f)), for the period given in section 4.
privacyNotice.purposes.i10: P16 — Technical providers: for your data, they act on instructions (art. 28) and have no basis of their own; what some of them also process on their own behalf is their own responsibility (section 6).
privacyNotice.purposes.p1: No purpose is based on a task carried out in the public interest. No decision producing legal effects is taken by automated means: the service decides no right.
privacyNotice.purposes.p2: Without an e-mail address no account can be created; optional fields can be left empty.
privacyNotice.purposes.p3_v8: The public page « Explore rights by need » (/droits) and the orientation questionnaire (/orientation), when it runs entirely in your browser, do their calculations in your browser: they send none of your answers to AccesDirectAide and store nothing, neither with us nor on your device. All that remains, as for any page of the site, are the host's usual technical logs of the pages requested (P1 above; retention in section 4, « Providers' technical logs »).
privacyNotice.purposes-later.title: 3a. Functions not open yet (proposed bases)
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i1: P4 — Searching for an appointment and showing the names of professionals: for you, performance of the terms (art. 6(1)(b)); for professionals, legitimate interest of the operator and of their structure (art. 6(1)(f)).
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i2: P4p — Professionals' accounts, including their two-step verification: legitimate interest (art. 6(1)(f)); performance of the professional terms they accept (art. 6(1)(b)).
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i3: P5 — Requesting, rescheduling, cancelling, confirming or declining an appointment, and the related service messages: performance of the terms (art. 6(1)(b)).
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i4: P5s — Appointment with a service whose nature may reveal health or disability data: performance of the terms (art. 6(1)(b)) and explicit consent (art. 9(2)(a)) through a separate box. This booking is not open.
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i5: P6 — Optional message attached to a request: consent (art. 6(1)(a)) and explicit consent (art. 9(2)(a)), which can be withdrawn at any time.
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i6: P7 — Assigning a professional to an appointment: performance of the terms (art. 6(1)(b)); « no preference » choice: legitimate interest of the structure (art. 6(1)(f)).
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i7: P8 — Referrals between professionals (closed feature): consent to each sharing (art. 6(1)(a); art. 9(2)(a)).
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i8: P9 — Shared files and follow-up (closed feature): consent to sharing (art. 6(1)(a); art. 9(2)(a)).
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i9: P10b/P10c — Reminder the day before and browser notifications: consent (art. 6(1)(a)), which can be withdrawn at any time.
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i10: P11 — Outlook availability of a structure (disabled): basis chosen by the structure; the operator acts on its behalf.
privacyNotice.purposes-later.p1: These processing operations are not in service. Their legal bases will be confirmed by the controller before they open; this notice will then be updated.
privacyNotice.retention.title: 4. Retention periods
privacyNotice.retention.i1: Account (e-mail address, protected password, display name, language, notification preferences, date of the last sign-in): as long as you use it. You can ask for its erasure at any time from your account: a person checks the request, to prevent a mistake or identity theft, then erases the account within one month at most.
privacyNotice.retention.proAccount_v9: ADA Pro professional account (professional e-mail address, role, structure, password in hashed form, two-factor authentication secret, notification preferences and, if you enter them, display name and job title): as long as you are a member of your structure's team. When you leave it, your structure's administrator, or the operator, disables the account: your sessions end at once. A disabled account is kept for 12 months at most, so that it can be reactivated and actions can be proven, then erased; this erasure is not automated yet: the operator carries it out from the administration console. You can ask for an earlier erasure by writing to {{contact}}. The erasure deletes your address, your password, your two-factor authentication, your preferences, your display name and job title, your notifications and your address in the invitations sent to you; the account keeps only its technical identifier, its role and its structure, which the logs refer to. When your structure's space is closed, the accounts of its team are erased in the same way. The proof of your acceptance of the terms for professionals (account identifier, document, version and date, without your address) is kept for 12 months after the erasure; this deletion is not automated yet.
privacyNotice.retention.proLinks_v9: Professional account — invitations, links and sessions: an invitation is valid for 7 days and once only, the two-factor activation link for 72 hours, the password reset link for 1 hour (it is kept at Upstash, in Frankfurt, during that hour). Of an invitation link we keep only a fingerprint, with the invited address and the role; an expired invitation is deleted 30 days after it expires — this deletion is not automated yet — and in any case it is erased or anonymised together with your account. Sign-in session: 12 hours at most. Beyond 5 sign-in attempts within 15 minutes from the same IP address or for the same e-mail address, further attempts are refused for 15 minutes at most.
privacyNotice.retention.proLogs_v9: Professional account — notifications, log and e-mails: notifications shown in ADA Pro are kept for 180 days; the log of your actions (date, action, structure, sign-in IP address; without your e-mail address) follows the rule for administration and security logs below (12 months). These deletions are not automated yet. The e-mails sent to you (invitation, password, notices) follow the « Service e-mails » rule above; however, the request to delete the address at Mailjet is not yet made for a professional account: the address Mailjet recorded when sending them may stay there under the « Providers' technical logs » rule.
privacyNotice.retention.i2: Inactive account: an account without any activity on your part (sign-in) for 24 months may be erased. This erasure is not in service yet; before it is, this notice will say how you will be warned. Account never activated (e-mail address never confirmed): erased together with the record of its sign-up no later than 8 days after its creation: the automatic erasure runs once a day as soon as the account is 7 days old.
privacyNotice.retention.i3: Address-verification, password and address-change links: valid for 15 minutes (30 minutes for an address change); an expired or already used link no longer works. We keep only a fingerprint of it (and, for an address change, the new address encrypted); their automatic deletion after expiry is not active yet: they are deleted with the account.
privacyNotice.retention.i4: Sign-in session: 7 days at most. After 5 failed sign-ins, the account is locked for 15 minutes.
privacyNotice.retention.i5: Rate-limiting counters (your IP address and, for sign-in, account creation and the sending of links, a fingerprint of your e-mail address, never the address itself): erased at the end of their window, from a few minutes to one hour. The logs keep only a condensed fingerprint of them.
privacyNotice.retention.i6: Service e-mails: AccesDirectAide does not keep their content; the record of the sending (the message number at the provider) is kept 12 months. If an address permanently refuses messages, a fingerprint of the address (not the address itself) blocks sending; this block is reviewed after 12 months and removed if it is no longer justified. When your account is erased, we ask Mailjet to delete the address it recorded, before erasing it on our side; when Mailjet confirms, it anonymises it at once and erases its records after 30 days. If it does not confirm, we try again for 3 days at most, without exceeding the one-month period for answering your request; if the failure persists, your account is erased on our side all the same, a person is alerted to intervene, and the address may stay at Mailjet under the rule stated below (providers' technical logs). For an account never activated, the request to Mailjet is made when it is automatically erased, with no further attempt. After a change of address, the same request is made for the old address, with no further attempt.
privacyNotice.retention.i7: Restricted-access archives after an account is erased: proof of acceptance of the terms of use and of the « 18 or over » statement, 12 months; requests to exercise rights, 3 years after they are closed. They serve only to prove or defend in a dispute.
privacyNotice.retention.i8: Consent decisions replaced by a more recent decision: 3 years after they were recorded.
privacyNotice.retention.i9: Help requests sent to support through the help form (not open yet), including to regain access to an account: 12 months after the request is closed.
privacyNotice.retention.i10: Administration and security logs (without your e-mail address): 12 months.
privacyNotice.retention.i11: Blocked retention (« hold ») of a specific item, when an authority requires it or a dispute calls for it: until the end of the procedure; the record of its release is kept 12 months.
privacyNotice.retention.i12: Providers' technical logs: the host (Vercel) keeps its runtime logs for 1 day on its Pro plan, and 30 days when its « Observability Plus » option is enabled for the site. The e-mail provider (Mailjet) keeps sending statistics for 90 days on Mailjet's free plan, 13 months on a paid plan; it records the recipient's address as a contact and keeps it as long as our Mailjet account exists, unless we delete it earlier; at the end of our contract, it erases the data within 90 days. Mailjet does not publish a period for the content of messages.
privacyNotice.retention.i13: Restoration history: encrypted backup copies, 35 days at most; database history at Neon, 6 hours at most on Neon's free plan, which we use. An erased item may remain in these copies for these periods; it is used only to repair an incident. So that a restoration cannot bring back an erased person, a record of each erasure (technical identifier of the account and of the request, date; no address or name) is kept for 40 days outside the database, at Upstash (Frankfurt).
privacyNotice.retention.i13_v7: Restoration history: encrypted backup copies, 35 days at most; database history at Neon, 6 hours at most on Neon's free plan, which we use. An erased item may remain in these copies for these periods; it is used only to repair an incident. So that a restoration cannot bring back an erased person, a record of each erasure (technical identifier of the account and of the request, date; no address or name) is kept for 40 days outside the database, at Upstash (Frankfurt). A second, encrypted copy of this record, which Cloudflare cannot read, is kept for 40 days at Cloudflare in the European Union.
privacyNotice.retention.i14: Functions not open yet (in particular appointments, optional message, professionals' notifications, assistant, household members, consultation history, favourites, tracking of procedures): their periods will be announced in this notice before they open. For confirmed, attended or missed appointments, the intended period is 1 year after the appointment date, then anonymisation.
privacyNotice.retention.i14_v9: Functions not open yet (in particular appointments, optional message, referrals between professionals, assistant, household members, consultation history, favourites, tracking of procedures): their periods will be announced in this notice before they open. For confirmed, attended or missed appointments, the intended period is 1 year after the appointment date, then anonymisation.
privacyNotice.retention.p1: None of these periods is imposed by a legal text: they are set by the controller. Automatic deletion at these deadlines is not yet fully switched on; you can ask for erasure at any time.
privacyNotice.recipients.title: 5. Recipients
privacyNotice.recipients.p1: Your data are neither sold nor rented. Access is given to: the operator; the technical providers of section 6, on instruction for your data (section 6 also states what some of them process on their own behalf).
privacyNotice.recipients.pro_v9: For a professional account, the administrators of your structure also see your professional address, your role, the status of your account, your notification preferences and the structure's log of actions, and can export them (export of the structure's data). Your display name and job title, if you enter them, are not published on the public site.
privacyNotice.recipients.p2: Once appointments open (they are not open yet), the structure you choose for an appointment will also receive what is passed on to it (section 9).
privacyNotice.processors.title: 6. Technical providers (processors)
privacyNotice.processors.i1: Vercel Inc.: hosting of the site and of the server functions, run in Frankfurt; the pages themselves (static content, no account data) are distributed by Vercel's global network.
privacyNotice.processors.i2: Neon (contract with Databricks, Inc.): database hosted in Frankfurt.
privacyNotice.processors.i3: Upstash, Inc.: security counters and request rate limiting, in Frankfurt.
privacyNotice.processors.i3_v7: Upstash, Inc.: security counters and request rate limiting, in Frankfurt. Upstash also keeps, in Frankfurt, the erasure records (section 4).
privacyNotice.processors.i3_v9: Upstash, Inc.: security counters and request rate limiting, in Frankfurt. Upstash also keeps, in Frankfurt, the erasure records (section 4) and, for 1 hour, the password reset links of professional accounts.
privacyNotice.processors.i4: Mailjet (Sinch group): sending of service e-mails (address verification, password, account notices); data hosted by Google Cloud in Frankfurt (Germany) and Saint-Ghislain (Belgium).
privacyNotice.processors.i4_v9: Mailjet (Sinch group): sending of service e-mails (address verification, password, account notices, invitations and notices of professional accounts); data hosted by Google Cloud in Frankfurt (Germany) and Saint-Ghislain (Belgium).
privacyNotice.processors.i5: Microsoft: inbox of the contact address.
privacyNotice.processors.i6: Scaleway SAS (France) and Cloudflare, Inc.: backup copies of the database. The backup task runs at Scaleway, in Paris, and encrypts the copy before it is sent anywhere; Cloudflare stores it in the European Union without being able to read it.
privacyNotice.processors.i6_v7: Scaleway SAS (France) and Cloudflare, Inc.: backup copies of the database. The backup task runs at Scaleway, in Paris, and encrypts the copy before it is sent anywhere; Cloudflare stores it in the European Union without being able to read it. Cloudflare also keeps, in the European Union and without being able to read it, the second, encrypted copy of the erasure records (section 4).
privacyNotice.processors.p1: For your data, each of these providers acts on instruction, as a processor, under a data processing agreement (GDPR Article 28) incorporated into its terms of service. Some of them also process, on their own behalf and under their own responsibility, technical data related to the use of their service, in particular: Vercel, for the usage data generated by its service; Sinch (Mailjet), to route messages, fight spam and fraud and secure its network; Upstash, for the security and analysis of its own service.
privacyNotice.transfers.title: 7. Transfers outside the European Union
privacyNotice.transfers.p1: Most of these providers belong to groups established in the United States; Mailjet belongs to the Swedish group Sinch, which has subsidiaries in the United States: access from the United States is possible. The safeguards provided are the European Commission's standard contractual clauses (Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914), incorporated into each provider's terms. Vercel Inc. and Upstash, Inc. are in addition on the official list of the EU–US Data Privacy Framework (consulted on 17 November 2026); Upstash relies first on this framework, and on the standard contractual clauses if it no longer applies. Databricks, Inc. (Neon) is also on that list. Scaleway SAS is the exception: it is a French company, which runs the backup task in Paris.
privacyNotice.rights.title: 8. Your rights
privacyNotice.rights.i1: Access, rectification, erasure and restriction of your data.
privacyNotice.rights.i2: Portability, for data processed on the basis of the terms of use or of your consent.
privacyNotice.rights.i3: Objection, for processing based on legitimate interest.
privacyNotice.rights.i4: Withdrawal of your consent at any time, as easily as you gave it. Withdrawal does not affect what was done before.
privacyNotice.rights.i5: Instructions on what happens to your data after your death (retention, erasure, disclosure): you may define them, under article 85 of the French loi Informatique et Libertés.
privacyNotice.rights.p1: From your space, you can yourself: download a copy of your data (export), correct your account information, request the erasure of your account and request the restriction of the use of your data.
privacyNotice.rights.pro_v9: For a professional account, these self-service functions do not exist: write to {{contact}} to access your data, obtain a copy, have it corrected or erased, or request its restriction. In ADA Pro, you can yourself change your display name, your job title and your notification preferences.
privacyNotice.rights.p2: You can also write to {{contact}}, for these rights as for the others. You receive an answer within one month.
privacyNotice.rights.p3: You can also lodge a complaint with the CNIL (www.cnil.fr).
privacyNotice.booking.title: 9. When you request an appointment (draft)
privacyNotice.booking.p1: Appointment requests are not open yet. What follows will apply once they are.
privacyNotice.booking.p2: The chosen structure will receive your name, your e-mail address, your telephone if you give it, the requested slot and, if you accepted, your message.
privacyNotice.booking.p3: For what it receives, the structure will be the controller of its own processing: it will decide what it does with it in its files, according to its obligations. You will be able to exercise your rights with it.
privacyNotice.booking.p4: For the handling of the request in the platform, the operator and the structure would be joint controllers; an arrangement will set this out and its essence will be published. No structure has signed an arrangement to date.
privacyNotice.sensitive.title: 10. Sensitive services (draft)
privacyNotice.sensitive.p1: Some services may reveal information about your health or a disability, for example a mental health or addiction service. An appointment request with these services would be processed only with your explicit consent, given through a separate unticked box. Withdrawing this consent would cancel the request.
privacyNotice.sensitive.p2: Booking these services is closed to date.
privacyNotice.art14.title: 11. Professionals and structure contacts (article 14)
privacyNotice.art14.p1: The directory contains information about structures and, where applicable, their professional contacts (name of the structure, address of the establishment, professional telephone and e-mail address, sometimes the name of a manager). It is not collected from you: it comes from official or public sources — FINESS, data·inclusion, the Annuaire de l'administration (Service-Public / DILA). Each listing shows its source and its date.
privacyNotice.art14.p2: Purpose: informing the public about the services that exist. Basis: legitimate interest (GDPR Article 6(1)(f)). Period: as long as the official source publishes the information; updated at each import.
privacyNotice.art14.p3: If your structure creates a professional account for you, it provides your name and professional address: sections 3 to 8 also apply to you.
privacyNotice.art14.p4: You can ask for a correction or object to the display of data about you: {{contact}}.
privacyNotice.art14.p3_v8: If a professional account is opened for you, it is through an invitation sent to your professional e-mail address by an administrator of your structure or by the operator. This account holds your professional e-mail address, your role, your structure, your password in hashed form (one-way), the secret of your two-factor authentication, the log of your actions and your notification preferences. Your acceptance of the terms of use for professionals (and, for a structure administrator, of the conditions for structures) is recorded with their version in the consent register; it is not a consent within the meaning of the GDPR. Sections 3 to 8 also apply to you.
privacyNotice.art14.p3_v9: If a professional account is opened for you, it is through an invitation sent to your professional e-mail address by an administrator of your structure or by the operator. This account holds your professional e-mail address, your role, your structure, your password in hashed form (one-way), the secret of your two-factor authentication, the log of your actions and your notification preferences, as well as, if you enter them, your display name and job title. Your acceptance of the terms of use for professionals (and, for a structure administrator, of the conditions for structures) is recorded with their version in the consent register; it is not a consent within the meaning of the GDPR. Sections 3 to 8 also apply to you, with the rules specific to professional accounts that they state: purpose and basis in section 3 (P4p), periods in section 4, recipients in section 5, exercise of your rights in section 8.
privacyNotice.language.title: 12. Reference language
privacyNotice.language.p1: Only the French version of this notice is legally authoritative; translations are an aid to understanding.
privacyNotice.purposes.p17_v10: P17 — Mon Parcours, the personal tracking of your procedures (a procedure chosen from a closed list of common procedures, a published public place if you choose one, the status you indicate, a deadline with the official page it relates to, the history of changes without text): performance of the terms of use (art. 6, 1, b). Mon Parcours records no free text and offers no procedure related to health, disability, sex life, an offence or criminal proceedings, the right of residence, violence suffered, child protection, a legal protection measure or a situation of extreme precariousness. Only you can see your steps: no organisation, no professional, no trusted person and no administrator sees them in the service. Deadline reminders are given only in the notifications of Mon Espace, never by e-mail or SMS for the time being.
privacyNotice.retention.parcours_v10: Mon Parcours: a step in progress is kept as long as you keep it; you can delete it at any time. A finished or abandoned step is deleted, with its history, 24 months after it was closed; a notice warns you in Mon Espace 30 days before, and you can download your data at any time. A deleted step may remain for up to 35 days in the backup copies (« Restore history » below). If a restore took place within that period, a step you had deleted could reappear: you would be told and could delete it again.
privacyNotice.retention.i14_v10: Functions not open yet (in particular appointments, optional message, professionals' notifications, assistant, household members, consultation history, favourites): their periods will be announced in this notice before they open. For confirmed, attended or missed appointments, the intended period is 1 year after the appointment date, then anonymisation.
cguCitoyen.account.parcours_v10: Mon Parcours: you can track there, yourself, procedures chosen from a list offered by the service, with, if you wish, a public place and a deadline. What you indicate there is declarative: it is neither an application, nor a filing, nor proof of a procedure, and it commits neither AccesDirectAide nor any organisation; only the competent organisation decides. Mon Parcours accepts no free text. You can delete a step at any time; a finished step is deleted 24 months after it was closed.
privacyNotice.retention.i14_v11: Functions not open yet (in particular appointments, optional message, referrals between professionals, assistant, household members, consultation history, favourites): their periods will be announced in this notice before they open. For confirmed, attended or missed appointments, the intended period is 1 year after the appointment date, then anonymisation.
cguCitoyen.publishing.i1_v12: Some functions allow you to publish a text (testimonial, story). You are its author and you are answerable for it; you publish only what you are free to publish.
cguCitoyen.publishing.i2_v12: Before any publication, the operator, who carries out the moderation themselves, reviews the text. They reject a text that is contrary to the moderation charter (« Moderation charter » page): information about health or a disability, contact details or details that make it possible to recognise a person, abusive, threatening or discriminatory remarks, advertising, misleading information or a promise of a right, off-topic text, and any unlawful content. In case of doubt about health or the recognition of a third party, the text is rejected and you can rewrite it.
cguCitoyen.publishing.i3_v12: You can withdraw your text at any time; it is then erased. A text that has not been reviewed within 60 days is withdrawn automatically.
cguCitoyen.publishing.i4_v12: By publishing, you authorise AccesDirectAide to display your text on the site free of charge, under the name or pseudonym chosen, for as long as you do not withdraw it. This authorisation is not transferred to third parties.
cguCitoyen.publishing.i5_v12: Reporting. Anyone, with or without an account, can report content that they consider unlawful or contrary to the moderation charter (privacy notice, section 13). A report never removes a text by itself: a person decides.
cguCitoyen.publishing.i6_v12: Time limits: acknowledgement of receipt of a report sent by e-mail within 2 working days; review of a pending text within 5 working days; security report (threat to the life or safety of a person, child in danger) within 24 hours, with a possible interim measure; other reports within 7 days; answer to an appeal within 15 working days.
cguCitoyen.publishing.i7_v12: Reasons and remedies. If your text is rejected or withdrawn, or if your participation is suspended, you receive a statement of reasons. You can contest it for six months, free of charge, from your space; the decision is re-examined and the answer states its reasons. You can also bring the matter before a court.
cguCitoyen.publishing.i8_v12: Repeated abuse. After a warning, publication — or the handling of your reports — may be suspended for 1 to 180 days in the case of manifestly unlawful content, or of manifestly unfounded reports or appeals, repeated within 12 months (privacy notice, section 13).
cguCitoyen.publishing.i9_v12: Danger to a person. If content suggests that an offence threatening the life or safety of a person has been committed or is likely to be committed, AccesDirectAide informs the authorities. In an emergency, call 112 (or 15, 17).
cguCitoyen.publishing.i10_v12: Age. These functions are reserved for people who declare that they are 18 or over.
cguCitoyen.deletion.participation_v12: Participation in a function (community, testimonials) may also be suspended on its own, without affecting the rest of the account, with the same safeguards (reasons and remedies in section 7a).
privacyNotice.status.expansion_v12: It also describes, when they are open, the participation functions (section 3b) and the way in which published content is reported and moderated (section 13).
privacyNotice.participation.events_v12: Academy events: registering for an event, cancelling your registration and receiving a reminder in the notifications of Mon Espace from 48 hours before the start: performance of the terms of use (art. 6, 1, b). If you so choose, a single accessibility need from a list (for example sign language interpreting): your explicit consent (art. 9, 2, a), given through a separate box that is never ticked in advance. Each agreement and each withdrawal is recorded as proof. You can withdraw this need at any time from « My events »; cancelling the registration also erases it. The organiser receives only numbers (how many people are registered, how many needs of each kind), never your name or your address.
privacyNotice.participation.testimonials: Testimonials: publishing your testimonial after review, under the first name or pseudonym you choose: your consent (art. 6, 1, a), given for each text through a box that is never ticked in advance, which you can withdraw at any time; the text and the name are then erased. Do not write anything about your health, a disability or another person: a text that mentions them is not published. Reports and review: legitimate interest (art. 6, 1, f).
privacyNotice.participation.stories_v12: Community stories: same rule, under a pseudonym that you choose and that is never publicly linked to your account. Leaving the community deletes your pseudonym and your stories.
privacyNotice.participation.p1_v12: These functions are reserved for the accounts of people who have declared that they are 18 or over. Their retention periods are given in section 4, their recipients in section 5, reports and moderation decisions in section 13.
privacyNotice.retention.events_v12: Events: the accessibility need is erased as soon as you cancel, and at the latest on the day after the end of the event; the registration is deleted 30 days after the end of the event (or after your cancellation if it comes first); the page of a finished event is deleted after 12 months.
privacyNotice.retention.content_v12: Testimonials and stories: a text that has not been reviewed within 60 days is withdrawn automatically (text erased, withdrawal of your agreement recorded); a published text stays online for as long as you do not withdraw it, and we will ask you to confirm it after 3 years (nothing is withdrawn without your answer or a decision); after a withdrawal or a rejection, the text is erased at once and the row that keeps the status and the dates, without the text, is deleted after 12 months; a report is deleted when the decision is taken, and at the latest after 90 days; a pseudonym with no published or pending story is deleted after 24 months without activity.
privacyNotice.retention.notices_v12: Reports sent without an account (« Report content » form): deleted 12 months after the decision, and kept for as long as an appeal is in progress.
privacyNotice.retention.proofs_v12: Proofs of agreement (testimonials, stories, accessibility need): according to the rule for consent decisions above.
privacyNotice.retention.decisions_v12: Moderation decisions, appeals and measures against abuse: erased 1 year after the file is closed. A decision is closed when the time limit for appeal and the measure have ended and no appeal is in progress (its appeals are erased with it); a warning, 12 months after it was given; a suspension, when it ends or is lifted.
privacyNotice.recipients.expansion_v12: What you choose to publish (testimonial, story, with the name or pseudonym chosen) is visible to everyone. Moderation is carried out by the controller themselves, a natural person, the only moderator named at the date of this version, with an administration account in their name protected by two-factor authentication. In the moderation tool, they see the text and the name or pseudonym chosen, never your e-mail address or your account, nor who reported a piece of content; the author does not learn who reported it either.
privacyNotice.processors.i4_v12: Mailjet (Sinch group): sending of service e-mails (address verification, password, account notices and, for published content, acknowledgements of receipt of reports, moderation decisions and answers to appeals); data hosted by Google Cloud in Frankfurt (Germany) and Saint-Ghislain (Belgium).
privacyNotice.rights.expansion_v12: Withdrawing a testimonial or a story, withdrawing an accessibility need, leaving the community: from your space, in a single action. The moderation decisions concerning you and your appeals are in « Moderation decisions ». The export of your data includes these items.
privacyNotice.moderation.title_v12: 13. Published content, reports and moderation decisions
privacyNotice.moderation.p1_v12: AccesDirectAide stores and publishes, at your request, the content you write (testimonials, stories). For this content, it provides a hosting service within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 on digital services.
privacyNotice.moderation.p2_v12: Reporting. Anyone, with or without an account, can report content that they consider unlawful or contrary to the moderation charter (« Moderation charter » page) or to the rules of section 7a of the terms of use for individuals, from the « Report content » page or by writing to the point of contact indicated in the legal notice. The report states why the content is a problem, where it is located (the address of the page), your name and your e-mail address — except for content endangering a child — and you declare in good faith that this information is accurate and complete. Account holders can also report from the page of the content. If you gave an address, you receive an acknowledgement of receipt, then the decision and the possible remedies. The name and address are used only for this; the author of the content never sees them. Basis: legitimate interest (art. 6, 1, f).
privacyNotice.moderation.p3_v12: Deciding. The controller, who carries out the moderation themselves, examines each report; no content is removed automatically and no decision is automated. A report that gives reason to fear a threat to the life or safety of a person is handled as a priority, within 24 hours; other reports, within 7 days. If it gives rise to suspicion of an offence of this kind, the authorities are informed. In case of immediate danger, call 112 (or 15, 17): AccesDirectAide is not an emergency service.
privacyNotice.moderation.p4_v12: Giving reasons. If your content is not published or is removed, or if your participation is suspended, you receive a statement of reasons: the measure and its duration, the facts, whether the decision follows a report, the rule applied or, for content judged unlawful, the legal provision concerned, the absence of automated means, and your remedies. It is sent to you by e-mail and remains in your space (« Moderation decisions »).
privacyNotice.moderation.p5_v12: Contesting. You can contest a decision free of charge for six months — whether you are the author of the content or the person who reported it — from your space or, without an account, with the reference and the code in your acknowledgement of receipt. When another person also carries out moderation, it is that person who re-examines the decision. At the date of this version, a single person carries out moderation: they re-examine the decision themselves, no earlier than 24 hours after your appeal, and the answer tells you so. The answer states its reasons. You can also bring the matter before a court.
privacyNotice.moderation.p6_v12: Repeated abuse. A person who repeatedly publishes manifestly unlawful content, or who repeatedly sends manifestly unfounded reports or appeals, first receives a warning; if this happens again within 12 months, publication, or the handling of their reports, may be suspended for a period of 1 to 180 days, set case by case (number, proportion, seriousness, intent). The person receives the reasons for it and can contest it. For a person without an account, the measure is recorded with a fingerprint of their address calculated with a secret key, never with the address itself.
privacyNotice.moderation.p7_v12: Rules applied. Rejected content, the time limits and the remedies are described in the moderation charter, published on the « Moderation charter » page, and in section 7a of the terms of use for individuals. No certified out-of-court dispute settlement body is offered.
privacyNotice.processors.i4_v13: Mailjet (Sinch group): sending of service e-mails (address verification, password, account notices, invitations and notices of professional accounts and, for published content, acknowledgements of receipt of reports, moderation decisions and answers to appeals); data hosted by Google Cloud in Frankfurt (Germany) and Saint-Ghislain (Belgium).
privacyNotice.processors.video_v13: Video conferencing: it is offered only for an appointment for which the structure has approved video conferencing and for which you have given your agreement; its basis is that of appointments (P5, section 3). AccesDirectAide then sends to 8x8 only an access token valid from 15 minutes before the start to 15 minutes after the end of the appointment, which contains a calculated room name (a string of characters that contains neither your name, nor the date, nor the structure), a technical identifier specific to the appointment, a generic display name (« Personne accompagnée » or « Conseiller·e ») and the role in the room; neither your name, nor your e-mail address, nor the subject of the appointment. During the call, your browser connects directly to the servers of 8x8: the sound, the image and the written messages in the room pass through them, and 8x8 receives the technical data of the connection (in particular your IP address). The call is not recorded: recording, live streaming, transcription, telephone calls and the sending of files are disabled.
privacyNotice.transfers.video_v13: Video conferencing: 8x8, Inc. is established in the United States; the video conferencing data may be transferred there. The safeguard provided is that of the European Commission's standard contractual clauses (Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914, module 2: controller to processor), provided for by 8x8's data processing agreement.
privacyNotice.processors.provider_v13: 8x8, Inc. (United States): video conferencing for appointments (the « Jitsi as a Service » service). 8x8 acts as a processor under its data processing agreement (« Global Data Processing Addendum », February 2025 version), incorporated into its terms of service.
privacyNotice.status.p1_v13: This notice describes the processing for personal accounts (section 3) and for ADA Pro professional accounts (section 3, P4p, and section 11). In ADA Pro, the following are open: the account, team and structure-record functions (with the structure's log and statistics), appointments (request, confirmation, rescheduling, cancellation, assignment to a professional), video conferencing for appointments and the reading of the Outlook availability (busy or free) of professionals who connect their calendar. Social referrals between structures (P23) and browser notifications (P10c) are also open. The message attached to a request, the reminder by e-mail the day before, referrals of files between professionals and the sharing of files are not open yet: their legal bases are given as proposals (section 3a) and will be confirmed before they open.
privacyNotice.purposes.p4p_v13: P4p — ADA Pro professional accounts (creation by invitation or upon a request to register a structure with its SIRET number, verified by the operator against an official source, sign-in with mandatory two-factor authentication, management of the team and invitations by the structure administrator, proposals to update the structure's record, optional display name and job title, notifications and service e-mails, log of actions): performance of the terms of use for professionals accepted at sign-up (Art. 6(1)(b)); account security and log of actions: legitimate interest of the operator and of the structure in protecting access (Art. 6(1)(f)).
privacyNotice.purposes.p11_v13: P11 — Outlook availability of a professional who connects their calendar (busy or free only): basis chosen by the structure; the operator acts on its behalf.
privacyNotice.retention.appointments_v13: Appointments: a confirmed, attended or missed appointment is anonymised 1 year after its date; a request that is declined, has expired or has remained unanswered is anonymised 90 days after the planned date of the appointment, and a cancelled appointment 90 days after its cancellation; the message attached to a request, when this function is open, is erased 30 days after the date of the appointment (or after the cancellation if it comes first).
privacyNotice.retention.outlook_v13: Outlook calendar of a professional: the connection tokens, encrypted, are kept as long as the connection is active; an expired token that has not been renewed is deleted 30 days after it expires. The busy or free slots that are read are not recorded in the database: they are kept for 2 minutes at most, in memory.
privacyNotice.retention.i14_v13: Functions not open yet (in particular optional message, reminder by e-mail the day before, referrals of files between professionals, household members, consultation history, favourites): their periods will be announced in this notice before they open.
privacyNotice.recipients.p2_v13: The structure you choose for an appointment also receives what is passed on to it (section 9). When a professional has connected their Outlook calendar, Microsoft receives the availability requests (busy or free) for that calendar; no information about you is sent to it.
privacyNotice.processors.i5_v13: Microsoft: inbox of the contact address; for professionals who connect their Outlook calendar, reading of only the busy or free slots of that calendar (« Calendars.ReadBasic » permission), without the subject, the participants or the location of the events; nothing is written to the calendar. Depending on the rules of the professional's Microsoft organisation, the agreement of their administrator may be required.
privacyNotice.booking.p1_v13: An appointment request is made from your account. Depending on the structure's choice, the appointment is confirmed immediately, or the structure confirms, offers another slot or declines.
privacyNotice.booking.p2_v13: In ADA Pro, the chosen structure receives the service, the slot and the format (on site or by video conference) that you chose and, when this function is open and you have accepted it, your message. The platform passes on to it neither your name, nor your e-mail address, nor your telephone; notices about the appointment are sent to you by the platform.
privacyNotice.booking.p3_v13: For what it receives, the structure is the controller of its own processing: it decides what it does with it in its files, according to its obligations. You can exercise your rights with it.
privacyNotice.booking.p4_v13: For the handling of the request in the platform, the operator and the structure are joint controllers (Article 26 of the GDPR). The essence of their arrangement: the operator runs the platform and handles the requests to exercise rights made through it; the structure is responsible for the appointment itself and its follow-up outside the platform. You can exercise your rights with either of them.
privacyNotice.art14.p3_v13: If a professional account is opened for you, it is through an invitation sent to your professional e-mail address by an administrator of your structure or by the operator, or following the request to register your structure that you made yourself (name of the structure, SIRET number, your professional e-mail address, a password and your acceptance of the terms of use for professionals). In that case, the account gives access to nothing until the operator has verified the structure against an official source and activated your space; you then receive an e-mail to activate your access with two-factor authentication. If the request is refused, the account is deactivated and the proof of your acceptance of the terms is kept. This account holds your professional e-mail address, your role, your structure, your password in hashed form (one-way), the secret of your two-factor authentication, the log of your actions and your notification preferences, as well as, if you enter them, your display name and job title. Your acceptance of the terms of use for professionals (and, for a structure administrator, of the conditions for structures) is recorded with their version in the consent register; it is not a consent within the meaning of the GDPR. Sections 3 to 8 also apply to you, with the rules specific to professional accounts that they state: purpose and basis in section 3 (P4p), periods in section 4, recipients in section 5, exercise of your rights in section 8.
cguPro.intro_v10: These terms apply to professionals who use an ADA Pro account, created at the invitation of an administrator of their structure or of the operator, or opened through the registration of their structure.
cguPro.account.i1_v10: The account is created through an invitation sent to your professional e-mail address by an administrator of your structure or by the operator (for example for the first administrator of a structure), or following a request to register your structure made by yourself, with its name, its SIRET number, your professional e-mail address, a password and your acceptance of these terms. In that case, the account gives access to nothing until the operator has verified the structure against an official source and activated its space; you then receive an e-mail to activate your access with two-factor authentication. If the request is refused, the account is deactivated and the proof of your acceptance is kept. The account is personal: do not share it.
cguPro.appointments.p1_v10: When appointment booking is open for your structure, you confirm, offer another slot or decline the requests addressed to you, within a reasonable time, and you keep your slots up to date.
cguPro.appointments.p3_v10: If your structure offers video conferencing for an appointment, its processing and its provider (8x8) are described in the privacy notice.
cguPro.appointments.p4_v10: If you connect your Outlook calendar, only your busy or free slots are read, so as not to offer a slot when you are busy; nothing is written to your calendar. You can disconnect it at any time.
cguPro.data.p1_v10: For your account, the platform processes your professional e-mail address, your role, your structure, your password in hashed (irreversible) form, the secret of your two-factor authentication, the log of your actions and your notification preferences, as well as, if you enter them, your display name and job title. When appointment booking is open for your structure, it also processes your slots and, if you connect your Outlook calendar, the encrypted connection tokens and your busy or free slots. This processing is based on the performance of these terms (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR) and, for account security and the log of actions, on the legitimate interest of the operator and of your structure in protecting access (Article 6(1)(f)). The privacy notice describes it (section 3, P4p and P11), with its retention periods (section 4) and how to exercise your rights (section 8).
structures.intro_v9: These conditions describe the rules proposed to structures (associations, public services, establishments) that appear in the directory, whose team uses ADA Pro accounts or that receive appointment requests.
structures.agreement.p1_v9: A structure receives appointment requests when it has opened appointment booking in its ADA Pro space. The connection is free: no sum is paid by the structure or to the structure.
structures.roles.p1_v9: For what it receives (requests and, when this function is open, message accepted by the person), the structure is the controller of its own processing, in its own files and according to its own obligations.
structures.roles.p2_v9: For the handling of an appointment request or a social referral in the platform, the operator and the structure are joint controllers (GDPR, art. 26). Their arrangement is as follows: the operator runs the platform and handles the requests to exercise rights addressed to it through the platform; the structure is responsible for the appointment or the support itself and its follow-up outside the platform. People can exercise their rights with either of them. The essence of this arrangement is made available to them in the privacy notice (section 9).
structures.commitments.i1_v9: Answer appointment requests within a reasonable time and keep its slots up to date.
structures.end.p1_v9: Either party may end the connection. The data are then processed according to the periods stated in the privacy notice.
privacyNotice.purposes.p4_v13: P4 — Searching for an appointment and showing the names of professionals: for you, performance of the terms (art. 6(1)(b)); for professionals, legitimate interest of the operator and of their structure (art. 6(1)(f)).
privacyNotice.purposes.p5_v13: P5 — Requesting, rescheduling, cancelling, confirming or declining an appointment, and the related service messages: performance of the terms (art. 6(1)(b)).
privacyNotice.purposes.p7_v13: P7 — Assigning a professional to an appointment: performance of the terms (art. 6(1)(b)); « no preference » choice: legitimate interest of the structure (art. 6(1)(f)).
cguCitoyen.noDecision.estimate_g14c: Amounts calculated from the questionnaire are indicative estimates: only the competent body decides.
cguCitoyen.ai.p1_g14c: The automatic assistant searches the verified pages, explains and cites its sources. It can make mistakes. It gives no medical or legal advice and decides nothing about your rights; in an emergency, call 112.
cguCitoyen.ai.p2_g14c: Do not write in it any information about your health, a disability, your administrative situation or that of another person.
cguCitoyen.account.assisted_g14c: Assisted mode: you can let a person of your choice help you in your account, next to you, for 2 hours at most, after entering your password; they can never change your security, delete the account or grant new access, and everything they do is recorded in a log that you can see. This mode does not replace a guardianship (tutelle), a curatorship (curatelle) or a mandate.
privacyNotice.purposes.p18_g14c: P18 — Indicative calculation of aid from the questionnaire: your answers (including, if you choose it, your municipality in the Eurométropole) are sent to our own OpenFisca calculation engine, hosted by Scaleway SAS in France, which acts as a processor; they are not stored there. The result is an indicative estimate: only the competent body decides. Basis: the operator's legitimate interest in informing the public (art. 6, 1, f).
privacyNotice.purposes.p19_g14c: P19 — Citizen assistant: your question and extracts of verified public pages are sent from our server to Cloudflare, Inc. (Workers AI service), which acts as a processor (art. 28); neither your IP address nor your account is passed on to it. E-mail addresses and telephone numbers are masked, and a question containing a social security number, an IBAN or a bank card number is refused. We do not store the conversation. The assistant gives no medical or legal advice, does not rule on your rights, cites its sources and reminds you of the emergency numbers. Basis: the operator's legitimate interest in informing the public (art. 6, 1, f).
privacyNotice.purposes.p20_g14c: P20 — Observatory of rights and services: during certain searches and consultations, the service counts, for the day, codes taken from closed lists and, except for sensitive subjects, the municipality; never your identity, your IP address, the time or any text. On « Ma situation », nothing is counted unless you tick « Aider l'Observatoire ». The daily counts are deleted when each quarter is closed; the quarterly tables, in which values below 5 are masked, are published under the Licence Ouverte 2.0. Basis: legitimate interest (art. 6, 1, f).
privacyNotice.purposes.p21_g14c: P21 — Assisted mode: at your request, a person who helps you (a relative, a social worker, a France Services adviser, a professional) uses your account next to you, for 2 hours at most, with your agreement, after you have entered your password. They can never change your security settings, delete the account, make the full export of your data or grant new access; Mon Coffre only if you ticked it, and never for a professional. A trusted person at a distance can only request actions that you confirm, unless you have allowed them to « agir pour moi » (act for me) for part of your space. Everything that is done is recorded in a log that you can see. This mode replaces neither a guardianship (tutelle), nor a curatorship (curatelle), nor a mandate; it is reserved for accounts of adults. Basis: your consent (art. 6, 1, a).
privacyNotice.purposes.situation_g14c: The « Ma situation » page (/situation) works in the same way: the words you type and the municipality you choose stay in your browser; they are neither sent nor stored. If you are signed in and choose « Ajouter à Mon Parcours », only the code of the procedure, taken from a closed list, is stored (P17). If you tick « Aider l'Observatoire », only the identifier of the chosen situation is sent, with nothing that identifies you (P20).
privacyNotice.purposes.offline_g14c: Mon Parcours offline: if you tick it, a copy of your steps is kept on your device, in your browser's storage, without encryption; do not enable it on a shared device. It is erased when you untick the box, when you sign out or when you change account; offline, it can only be read. The site also keeps public technical files on the device. This storage is strictly necessary for the service you request (article 82 of the French Data Protection Act, loi Informatique et Libertés): it does not ask for any other agreement.
privacyNotice.purposes.passeport_g14c: The Passeport Social is kept encrypted on your device only: AccesDirectAide receives nothing from it and cannot recover it; if you lose the device or its key, it is lost. You alone decide whether to show it or pass it on. It is not a processing by AccesDirectAide.
privacyNotice.retention.assistant_g14c: Citizen assistant: no conversation is stored; anonymous technical counters are kept for 90 days. Indicative calculation (P18): your answers are not stored.
privacyNotice.retention.assisted_g14c: Assisted mode: the log of what was done with the help of another person is kept for 1 year; your agreement follows the rule for consent decisions above.
privacyNotice.retention.observatory_g14c: Observatory: the daily counts are deleted when the quarter is closed; the published quarterly tables contain no personal data.
privacyNotice.retention.i14_v12: Functions not open yet (in particular appointments, optional message, professionals' notifications, household members, consultation history, favourites): their periods will be announced in this notice before they open. For confirmed, attended or missed appointments, the intended period is 1 year after the appointment date, then anonymisation.
privacyNotice.processors.cloudflare_g14c: Cloudflare, Inc. (Workers AI service): answers of the citizen assistant, from the question and extracts of public pages sent by our server. Cloudflare states that it does not use this content to train models and does not keep it after the answer for an ordinary request.
privacyNotice.processors.scaleway_g14c: Scaleway SAS (France): hosting of our OpenFisca calculation engine, in Paris; the answers to the questionnaire are not stored there.
privacyNotice.transfers.cloudflare_g14c: Citizen assistant: Cloudflare, Inc. is established in the United States. Its data processing agreement (version 6.4 of 3 April 2026) provides for the standard contractual clauses of the European Commission (Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914, module 2: controller to processor), and Cloudflare declares that it complies with the EU–US Data Privacy Framework.
privacyNotice.purposes.p10c_g14c: P10c — Browser notifications (Web Push), if you turn them on: a short encrypted reminder goes through the notification service of your browser's publisher (Apple, Google, Mozilla or Microsoft), which may be located outside the European Union; it contains neither your name, nor the structure, nor any health information. The e-mail remains the notice that counts. The calendar file (.ics) contains only the date, the time and the public address of the place, and only for a service that is not sensitive. Basis: your consent (art. 6, 1, a), which can be withdrawn at any time.
privacyNotice.purposes.p23_g14c: P23 — Social referral to another structure (outside health): a professional proposes a referral to you and you confirm it in Mon Espace with a single-use code. The following are processed: the sending and receiving structures, reasons taken from a closed list, the status of the referral and, if you tick it, your e-mail address or your telephone number, which only the receiving structure sees while the referral is in progress. No document and no health information. You can withdraw your agreement at any time. For the handling of the referral in the platform, the operator and the structures are joint controllers, under the arrangement described in section 9. Basis: your consent (art. 6, 1, a).
privacyNotice.purposes-later.p10b_g14c: P10b — Reminder by e-mail the day before: consent (art. 6, 1, a), which can be withdrawn at any time.
privacyNotice.retention.socialReferrals_: Social referrals: 12 months after the referral is closed; your agreement and its withdrawal follow the rule for consent decisions above.
privacyNotice.retention.push_g14c: Browser notifications: the subscription is kept until you turn notifications off or your account is erased; a subscription that no longer works is deleted 30 days later.
privacyNotice.transfers.push_g14c: Browser notifications: the notification service of your browser's publisher may be located outside the European Union; it only passes on an encrypted reminder, which it cannot read.
